recipes.name: Easy Tuna Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine cooked macaroni, tuna, and condensed soup together in a 9x13-inch baking dish; sprinkle with cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly, about 25 minutes. Sprinkle with fried onions; bake 5 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Tuna Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This tuna pasta casserole is made with macaroni, creamy chicken soup, and Cheddar cheese. Top with crispy fried onions for a very comforting meal.

review.reviewBody:
The recipe's fine as is. I don't understand the need on the part of some to completely re-write the recipe. If you do that, you've created a NEW recipe, so why bother rating this one, as is? (Am I gonna be banned/kicked off the recipe.com site now for pointing out rudeness?) Just curious. :) 

This is a new take on the tuna casserole recipe. You either like it or you don't. I think it's fine, as written. Thank you to the creator for posting their creation.

SOOO GOOD! I used 4 C of cooked macaroni, 2 cans of tuna, one can cream of chicken soup, one can of cream of mushroom soup, 1/4 C of milk, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, blackpepper powder, 2 TBSP mayonnaise, and 1 tsp of dijon mustard. I put some cheddar cheese with the pasta mixture and put on top a combination of cheddar cheese and Italian mix cheese. On top of that, I melted 4 TBSP of butter, combined with 8 TBSP of seasoned bread crumbs and sprinkled on top of the cheese. This is totally Da Bomb!

From the start, I heeded the advice of other reviewers: added one can of mushroom soup, an extra can of tuna, half a can of milk, and a can of peas. I tasted the mixture at that point, and it was pretty good. For extra flavor, I added lemon pepper, garlic powder, dry mustard, and basil. I was generous with everything but the mustard. I used lowfat soups and omitted the cheese to save a few fatgrams, and it was still delicious, and easy, too!

The handiest tips I gathered from pouring through the reviews -- 2 cups uncooked macaroni = 3 cups cooked as called for; and, 1/2 soup can of milk made a great consistency. Excellent -- comfort dining at its finest!

So, I did change the recipe, but I think this would be great even without the changes. I added an extra can of tuna, a can of cream of mushroom soup because my husband likes mushrooms, a sprinkling of lemon pepper, salt, pepper and onion powder and lastly- 1/4 C of sour cream. Basically, I added the tuna/cream of mushroom for taste/creaminess, the spices to balance out the extra tuna and the sour cream because it was in my fridge and would have gone bad otherwise. This is a great base recipe that I bet tastes good on its own, but tastes absolutely awesome with my additions. Creamy, but not overwhelmingly fishy. Reminds me a little of Tuna Helper, but is not nearly as salty and a heck of a lot creamier/sturdier. Feel free to mess around with this recipe, I don't think you can mess it up.

We boiled a 16 oz of Amish Egg Noodles (Wide). We added a small bag of mixed frozen veggies in the last 6 minutes of boil time for pasta. Used 2 cans of white albacore tuna (drained) 2 cans of cream of celery. We heated the soup with 1/2 cup of milk and melted the cheese added garlic and onion powder. Crushed 1 cup of potato chips and probably 3/4 cup of Funyons with 2T melted butter. Put everything except potato chip mixture in 9x13 pan mixed it all up and then topped with chip mixture. Baked at 375 for 15 minutes. It was awesome and absolutely delicious!
The cheese shouldn't be put on at the beginning of the baking process! It just hardens it. Put on when putting on the fried onikns

I was really longing for the taste of this old family favorite. The thing is, neither my brother, nor I recall that there was ever cheddar cheese in it. However, I followed the recipe and used the cheese as directed. I didn’t have any onions to put on top so I used Panko crumbs and drilled a little butter over them. It’s satisfied my craving for this old dish. If this is a memory of yours, you have got to try it!

We very much enjoyed the final product, but we had to make changes based on other reviews and serving size. I used rotini pasta instead of macaroni, which was supposed to substitute in the same amounts. However, even though I doubled the tuna, doubled the soup and added 2 cups of cooked, diced broccoli, this did not fill the 9x13 casserole sufficiently, and I knew that it would not serve 8 people, like the recipe states. So I added 2 more cups of cooked rotini. The 5 cups total was the perfect amount for our family, serving 6-7. I also added spices - 1/4 tsp pepper, 1 tsp onion powder, 1/4 tsp garlic powder. As suggested by other reviews, I waited to sprinkle on the cheese until the last 5 minutes, just before adding the crispy onions. Crispy onions were difficult to find, but definitely a great aspect, adding a nice crunch to the top.

I used this as my base recipe for Tuna Casserole. I made this during this weeks Jan, 2026 heavy winter storm and I was out of a lot of what I thought usually I would have on had to make this. I ended up using 3x the tuna drained, 1x can of cream of mushroom soup, 1/2 jar of bottled mushrooms drained, 1/4 cup of plain Greek yogurt because the mix to tuna and pasta was dry. I added pepper, salt, onion powder and garlic powder. I thought I had French’s fried onions, but no. In lieu of the French’s fried onions, I griddled a large onion in bacon fat to glaze stage, chopped up about a heaping 1/4 cup with about a 1/3 cup of Panko for the topping. The cheese as instructed. I also used more pasta than called for. It was good pantry make do casserole.
I can't eat tuna so I used canned chicken. I added frozen peas. Definitely a keeper. Easy, filling and delicious 😋

I used the one 1X recipe, and after reading other reviews I decided to add diced onions, black olives, green olives with the pimentos inside, and seasoned it with "Garlic Sea Salt with Parsley," to add extra flavor. Also I baked it in my countertop "Elite Gourmet "oven, which eliminated heating up my kitchen.
Very quick and easy, need a quick one like this during these times!
This was so quick and easy and tasted great!
Made it as written, good 👍🏻 Made again added cream of mushroom soup, minced onion, onion powder, peas and Old Bay Seasoning. Even better 😀
This was a good and easy recipe I didn't have the onion to put on top, but it was fine without it

I used 3 cans of tuna and 2 chicken soups, added garlic salt and pepper to mine it really helps using milk and also add the cheese with the fried onion rings at the same time, this helps with the cheese not being so hard. My husband enjoyed it but might use peas next time. ALL in all was delicious.
Its okay, nothing special. Definitely something quick to make. The written direction should mention to rinse macaroni with cold water and the words sprinkle I find misleading. Its more like layer.
Onion powder in the mix, everyone loved it. Will make again!
Doubled the recipe and had medium egg noodles for the pasta. THIS was a hit with me and the hubby, and it'll be on the weekly rotation!
